summary: Found live on the rented Mac Mini M4 during the 1.3.0 macOS validation run (MPI-391 section C).

MPI-444 checked the dangling-connector half against scripts/build-portable.mjs and it is CONFIRMED, code-verified: copyAppTree (scripts/build-portable.mjs:367-378) re-creates a symlink verbatim with fs.symlink(linkTarget, targetPath) and only falls back to staging the resolved file when that call THROWS (Windows without symlink privilege). On the macOS runner fs.symlink succeeds for a nonexistent target, so node_modules/@cubric/connector ships as a dangling link pointing at ../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector, which no artifact contains. @cubric/connector is a prod dependency, so --omit=dev does not drop it. MEASURED AND IMPORTANT: moving it to optionalDependencies does NOT fix this - npm 11.9.0 still creates the dangling symlink and still exits 0 (repro run 2026-08-04). npm ci also does NOT fail on the missing file: target in either position, which is why MPI-444 needed no package.json change for CI. So the two real fixes here are: skip dangling symlinks in copyAppTree, or drop @cubric/connector from package.json entirely and install it as a dev-only extra.

note: Gate C split: symlink half shipped, CLT half deferred behind a known-issue line. See brief.md.
